review_candidates.title: Senior People Experience Specialist
review_candidates.description: About Khazna Khazna launched in 2020 with a mission to improve the financial well-being of the underbanked, who have little access to formal financial services by providing access to convenient, effective and secure smartphone-based financial services. Khazna has received the Central Bank of Egypt’s first prepaid card license and aims to become the go-to neobank for underbanked consumers across the Middle East. In the next phase of its journey, Khazna is looking to continue scaling up its operations in Egypt and to launch its operations in Saudi Arabia. This is a fun stage in the company's lifecycle as the core foundation has been laid, but it is still early enough to assume a ton of ownership and to help shape the future of the company and its success. Role Overview Khazna is a fast-growing fintech operating across Egypt and Saudi Arabia. The People Experience team sits within the wider People & Culture function and supports the business across Talent Management, HR Business Partnering, Talent Acquisition, employee engagement, and related people services. This is a senior individual contributor role focused primarily on Learning & Development, employee engagement, onboarding, and employee communications related to engagement and culture. The role is designed for someone who combines practical L&D and engagement experience with strong operational discipline and follow-through, turning plans into consistent, timely, well-documented programs and employee experiences. It also supports Performance Management and Talent Management cycles and provides a development path into broader HR Business Partnering, Employee Relations, and Talent Acquisition scope as capability and organizational need evolve. Key Responsibilities What This Role Owns: Learning & Development Own the training needs analysis process — run it with managers across individual, team, and organizational needs, and turn the findings into a clear view of where capability gaps sit. Own the annual L&D plan, calendar, and operating rhythm, while aligning priorities, audiences, delivery approach, owners, timing, and dependencies with the People & Culture Manager. Design, adapt, and facilitate in-house learning programs and workshops where appropriate; maintain reusable learning materials; and brief internal subject matter experts facilitating sessions. Experience building structured learning content from scratch is a strong advantage. Evaluate learning through feedback, participation, application, and follow-up; report on impact and uptake; and continuously improve the learning offer. Support in maintaining visibility of L&D activity, budget requirements, vendors, logistics, attendance, and outstanding actions. Engagement & Exit Support in building the engagement calendar and owning delivery of interactive engagement initiatives end-to-end — concept, planning, budget, logistics, communication, execution, participation tracking, and follow-up. Translate engagement findings and employee feedback into visible programs, events, campaigns, manager actions, and employee experiences. Own the exit interview process for assigned populations, including regular analysis of trends and themes. Support engagement survey analysis with the wider team, then own the activation and follow-through of agreed initiatives. Onboarding Experience Own the onboarding process and employee experience from pre-joining through probation completion, ensuring every new joiner receives a consistent, timely, and well-coordinated experience. Support in building and maintaining clear manager and team onboarding expectations, including structured Day 30, Day 60, and Day 90 checkpoints, role integration, probation reviews, required documentation, completion evidence, and clear ownership of actions. Track onboarding and probation milestones, follow up proactively with managers and employees, maintain completion evidence and records, and escalate delays, concerns, or cases requiring intervention to the relevant HRBP. Use employee and manager feedback, completion data, and recurring issues to continuously improve the onboarding framework and experience. What This Role Supports: Performance Management Administer the performance review cycle — system setup, launch communications, manager guidance, completion tracking — to the approach and timeline set by the People & Culture Manager. Prepare calibration materials and support the sessions. Support managers in turning review outcomes into development actions, maintain cycle documentation and follow-up, and feed process improvements back to the People & Culture Manager. Talent Reviews & Career Frameworks Support the implementation, communication, maintenance, and periodic review of Talent Management frameworks designed and governed by the People & Culture Manager and HR leadership. Employee Relations & Talent Acquisition Support employee relations matters with guidance from the People & Culture Manager. Support Talent Acquisition when additional team capacity is needed, including participating in recruitment activity where appropriate. Talent Acquisition experience is useful but not required. Reporting Support reporting and operating dashboards for learning, engagement, onboarding, exit, and development activity, with clear observations, actions, deadlines, and follow-up. Act as a senior point of reference on L&D, engagement, onboarding, and recurring People Experience processes, sharing practical guidance and good practice with the People Experience Specialists. Growth Path The role is expected to deepen ownership of its core employee-experience and development areas while progressively gaining broader exposure to the People disciplines already established within the team. Build increasingly sophisticated engagement, onboarding, and L&D practices, including stronger measurement, manager enablement, content design, vendor management, and programme improvement. Take on greater responsibility within Performance Management and Talent Management cycles, with deeper exposure to HR Business Partnering, Employee Relations, and Talent Acquisition. Requirements Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Human Resources, Psychology, or a related field. 5+ years of HR / People experience, with strong practical depth in Learning & Development, employee engagement, onboarding, employee experience, or a closely related area. Practical experience designing, adapting, and facilitating learning interventions directly. Experience creating structured learning content or programmes from scratch is a strong advantage. Experience supporting structured People cycles such as performance, talent, onboarding, or development, with evidence of strong process discipline and follow-through. Comfortable working with people's data and turning it into clear, practical analysis and actions. Confident working directly with managers and department heads, particularly on development, onboarding, and engagement. Demonstrated operational discipline: able to manage calendars, simple budgets, vendors, logistics, communications, documentation, deadlines, and recurring follow-up consistently. Experience planning and delivering employee engagement initiatives, events, campaigns, or employee-experience programmes is strongly preferred. Experience owning or materially improving onboarding and probation processes is strongly preferred. Exposure to Talent Management frameworks, talent reviews, succession planning, or career architecture is a big advantage. Experience handling employee relations matters and exposure to Talent Acquisition are advantages.

Overview Of The Role Support the Financial Planning & Analysis function for Cairo Festival City Mall by providing financial analysis, reporting and insights that support management decision-making. The role supports the full planning and analysis cycle, including budgeting, forecasting, monthly reporting, variance analysis and performance monitoring across mall revenues, occupancy, leasing and operating costs. Working closely with Leasing, Marketing, Operations, Development, Treasury and Finance teams, the position helps ensure accurate financial information, effective business partnering and commercially focused decision support. What You Will Do Support the monthly financial close for the Mall business, including review of accruals and accounting entries such as service charges, utilities, marketing and maintenance costs, and support balance sheet reconciliations. Analyze Mall P&L, Balance Sheet and Cash Flow performance against budget, forecast and prior year, highlighting key drivers, risks, opportunities and recommended actions. Develop and maintain financial models for budgeting, rolling forecasts and scenario analysis using updated leasing, occupancy and operational assumptions. Prepare Mall cash flow forecasts and monitor cash position in coordination with Treasury to identify funding requirements and surplus cash. Monitor OPEX and CAPEX performance against approved budgets and support the financial review of related purchase requests and tenders for budget alignment. Support monthly performance reviews, variance reporting, financial insights and improvement initiatives to help guide the financial direction of the Mall business. Prepare reports and schedules required by local, regional and Group Finance teams, ensuring business decisions are supported by accurate financial data. Act as a key link between Leasing, Marketing, Operations and Development teams and Local Finance, Shared Services Finance, Treasury, Regional Finance and Group Finance. Review lease agreements and analyze leasing performance, including tenant sales, occupancy cost ratios, occupancy levels, footfall, turnover rent, tenant incentives and collection performance. Provide financial evaluations for new Mall initiatives, projects, asset repositioning plans and investment decisions. Support internal and external audit requests and finance-related inquiries. Support finance improvement initiatives, including reporting automation, dashboards, KPIs and enhancements to planning and reporting systems such as SAP, SAC, Yardi and Power BI. Experience in Retail Real Estate / Shopping Malls is highly preferred. Strong knowledge of management reporting, budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis and financial modelling. Strong understanding of shopping mall business drivers and KPIs, including tenant sales, occupancy cost ratio, occupancy, footfall, turnover rent and service charges. Knowledge of accounting standards and financial statement preparation, with strong understanding of EAS / IAS / IFRS. Strong analytical thinking, attention to detail and the ability to translate financial information into clear business insights. Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with finance and non-finance stakeholders. Knowledge of ERP financial software is required; SAP and Yardi experience is preferred. Advanced Excel and Power BI skills are preferred. Commercially oriented and process-driven, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, take ownership of deliverables and perform effectively under pressure. What Equips You For The Role Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics or Commerce. Professional certification such as CMA or FMVA is preferred. Knowledge of management reporting, automation and accounting systems. Understanding of Egypt real estate laws, guidelines and directives is desirable. Ability to approach problem-solving with simplicity and logic and communicate financial matters effectively to non-finance professionals. Ability to think holistically and understand the wider business impact of financial transactions and decisions. About Al-Futtaim Group Real Estate The real estate development and operations arm of Al-Futtaim, Al-Futtaim Group Real Estate is responsible for a multi-billion-dollar portfolio across MENA. With high-quality residential, business, retail, tourism, educational and healthcare developments, the master developer caters to the diverse needs of cities and communities in the region. From origination, conception, development, sales, procurement and construction of mega-projects and the leasing, operation and management of these projects after completion, Al-Futtaim Group Real Estate (AFGRE) has been developing and managing owned landbanks, unlocking the economic potential of the region and contributing to future development for more than 40 years. Our focus is to enable and invest in meaningful relationships to make our properties the best places to live and work, build additional products and services and enable partnerships to create true value to our customers throughout their entire experience with us. AFGRE is responsible for master planning of all projects in its portfolio, including two large scale mixed use destinations: Dubai Festival City and Cairo Festival City.

THE ROLE Everpure Cloud Dedicated (formerly Cloud Block Store) is Pure’s enterprise storage solution running in the public cloud. It brings the same features customers know from FlashArray - like data reduction (deduplication and compression), snapshots, encryption, and replication - directly into AWS and Azure. Because we reduce how much data actually needs to be stored and how many native cloud disks are required, customers can run their workloads in the cloud with lower storage cost and predictable performance instead of over‑provisioning native cloud volumes. The service has been in production since 2019, serving enterprise, SaaS, and multicloud customers. It also acts as the storage engine for other Everpure Cloud offerings, such as Everpure Cloud Azure Native, where Azure users consume Pure storage as a native Azure service. Our Prague‑based team owns the project on both AWS and Azure end‑to‑end. We design and build the core storage architecture, handle resiliency and performance work, and drive deployment and upgrade mechanisms. We also work closely with product managers, support, and field teams on customer issues and roadmap priorities. Because we run on top of AWS and Azure, we must deeply understand their building blocks (VMs, disks, networking, databases) and how Purity behaves on top of them. For this role, we are looking for engineers who are curious about how things really work in the cloud, enjoy solving complex distributed‑systems problems, and are comfortable in a fast‑changing environment. Unlike traditional hardware projects, our work has to keep pace with new cloud services and features. You will help us evaluate new AWS and Azure capabilities and integrate them into our product to improve resiliency, performance, and cost efficiency for customers - while keeping the familiar, “FlashArray‑like” experience that Pure is known for. What You'll Do Design, implement, and review new features in the Everpure Cloud Dedicated data path, primarily in C++ and/or Python, running on AWS and Azure. Improve the resiliency, performance, and cost efficiency of our cloud storage stack (failover behavior, HA, capacity expansion, data reduction, cloud‑specific optimizations). Participate in our triage rotation: analyze failures from CI pipelines and automated tests, debug issues on CBS testbeds, and drive fixes into the codebase. Lead or co‑lead the investigation of product issues in customer environments, from initial escalation through root‑cause analysis and long‑term fixes. What You Bring Solid basis in software engineering foundation building and maintaining backend or system‑level components in production. Strong programming skills in C++ or Python and a willingness to pick up new languages, tools, and frameworks as needed. End‑to‑end ownership mindset – from design and implementation through tests, CI pipelines, deployment, monitoring, and iterative hardening in production. Strong debugging and problem‑solving skills, including working with complex logs, CI failures, and issues that cross service boundaries, APIs, and cloud components. review_candidates.title: Management Consulting Intern
review_candidates.description: 📝 Management Consulting Intern (Unpaid) ⚠️ Applications will only be accepted through the following site: 👉 www.owlera.site About Owlera Owlera is an AI-powered career platform that helps students and fresh graduates gain practical experience through internship simulations inspired by real companies. Participants work on realistic business challenges, receive AI-powered feedback, use modern professional tools, and build portfolio-ready projects that demonstrate their abilities to future employers. We're looking for sharp, structured, and driven students to join our Management Consulting Internship and learn how consultants solve real business problems — from framing the question to delivering boardroom-ready recommendations under pressure. About the Internship As a Management Consulting Intern, you'll work on realistic consulting engagements — diagnosing client problems, building fact packs, benchmarking performance, and crafting recommendations for realistic company scenarios. You'll learn how consultants work — hypothesis-led analysis, structured communication, the pyramid principle, data-driven insight generation, and turning complexity into clear, actionable advice. Responsibilities * Frame business problems with structured issue trees and hypothesis trees. * Build fact packs: collect, clean, and synthesize data into clear exhibits. * Benchmark client performance against industry peers and best practices. * Develop hypotheses and test them with data and targeted research. * Analyze processes and identify operational improvement opportunities. * Build business cases with cost-benefit framing and sensitivity checks. * Map stakeholders and understand decision-making dynamics. * Draft structured memos and one-pagers using the pyramid principle. * Design slide decks that tell a clear story with a "so what" on every page. * Interview realistic client stakeholders and synthesize key takeaways. * Run SWOT, five-forces, and value-chain analyses for realistic scenarios. * Pressure-test recommendations with risks, assumptions, and alternatives. * Present findings in realistic client-style update meetings. * Collaborate with other interns on team-based case engagements. * Track progress against milestones in a consulting-style work plan. Requirements * Current student or recent graduate in Business, Economics, Engineering, or a related field — or a strong self-taught portfolio of projects. * Strong interest in management consulting and structured problem-solving. * Analytical thinking with comfort around data, frameworks, and trade-offs. * Clear, concise writing — able to turn analysis into recommendations. * Comfort working with ambiguity and sharpening vague client questions. * Self-motivated and able to work independently under tight deadlines. * Strong communication skills and professional polish. * Familiarity with spreadsheets and slide decks is a plus. * Previous consulting experience is not required. What You'll Gain * Hands-on experience working like a management consultant, not just theory. * Practical skills in problem structuring, analysis, and recommendation design. * Understanding of how consultants diagnose problems and influence decisions. * Practical exposure to case work, fact packs, and client-style presentations. * Portfolio-ready consulting artifacts built on realistic business use cases. * Personalized AI feedback on your work. * Professional certificate upon successful completion. * Mentorship and weekly learning sessions. * Opportunity to strengthen your portfolio, resume, and interview readiness. Internship Details Role: Management Consulting Intern Location: Remote Type: Internship (Unpaid) Level: Entry Level Duration: 6 Weeks Commitment: Flexible (approximately 10–15 hours per week) If you love structured problem-solving, data-driven analysis, and delivering recommendations that matter — and want to learn how real consulting engagements run end to end — we'd love to hear from you. ⚠️ Apply through: 👉 www.owlera.site
